sentences.text: The above case is chargesheeted alleging offences punishable under Sections 120B, 406, 408 and 420 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

The petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 3.
2.

The prosecution case is that the petitioners in Annexure-I chargesheet issued a cheque for Rs.33,500/- drawn on Punjab National Bank in favour of M/s.Sreelakshmi Agencies and the cheque was returned unpaid due to insufficiency of funds.
The defacto complainant was running a coconut oil mill by name Sreelakshmai Agencies.

The 2nd accused, who is one of the partner of M/s.Trado Traders and who is working as the Manager of the defacto complainant's oil mill had taken away Rs.86,000/-, some documents, and office files from the office of the defacto complainant on 17.07.2013.
Based on the above allegation, a private complaint was filed by the defacto complainant before the jurisdictional court as evident by Annexure-II.
The learned Magistrate forwarded the complaint to the police under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C and the police registered the case as Crime No.1509/2013.
Consequently, Annexure-I final report is filed.

According to the petitioners,
even if the entire allegations are accepted, the offences alleged are not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
3. Heard Counsel for the petitioners and the public prosecutor.

4. The counsel for the petitioners submitted that, in Annexure-I charge sheet, the only allegation against the petitioners is that, they being the partners of M/s.Trado Traders, issued a cheque to the defacto complainant's firm for Rs.33,500/- and it is dishonoured for the reason that insufficient fund.

It is also submitted that, there is no case in Annexure-I final report to the effect that, on 17.07.2013, the 2nd accused had taken away Rs.86,000/- and other documents from the office of the defacto complainant with the knowledge and consent of the petitioners.
According to the petitioners, there is business transaction between the firm of the petitioners and the firm of the defacto complainant.
It is also submitted that, there is no case for the defacto complainant regarding the entrustment of any property or dishonestly misappropriating or converting the property by the petitioners.
The only grievance of the defacto complainant against the petitioners is that the cheque issued by the firm of the petitioners was dishonoured due to insufficiency of funds.

According to the petitioners, the dishonour of cheque due to insufficiency of funds in the account is not a ground to proceed against the petitioners under Sections 406 and 408 IPC.
5.

The public prosecutor submitted that the contentions of the petitioners are all matter of evidence and the petitioners has to adduce evidence to prove the same before the trial court at the appropriate stage.

sentences.text: Even though the defacto complainant was implicated as 2nd respondent in this Criminal Miscellaneous case and notice was issued to him, he refused to appear before this Court.
7. This court perused the final report.
After going through the final report and the documents produced by the prosecution, I am of the considered opinion that, there is some force in the argument of the petitioners.
The prosecution case is mainly regarding the dishonor of a cheque.
8. There are business transaction between the petitioners and the 2nd respondent.
The allegations of the prosecution are all financial transaction between the petitioners and the 2 nd respondent.
No criminal offence is made out against the petitioners.
Moreover, there is no appearance also for the 2 nd respondent in this Criminal Miscellaneous Case which is filed to quash the proceedings.
That itself show that the 2nd respondent is also not interested to proceed against the petitioners.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal prosecution is not necessary.
If there is any monitory dispute, the defacto complainant is free to approach the competent civil court.
9. With the above observation, the criminal prosecution against the petitioners can be quashed.
Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioners in C.C.No.668/2016 on the file of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-IX, Ernakulam,
arising from crime No.1509/2013 of Palarivattom Police Station are quashed.
